scope: Proposition 11.6 (Sixteen time blocks from averaged input lists) of the manuscript “Random coordinate frames and partial permutation laws” (preprints/Random-coordinate-frames-and-partial-permutation-laws-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0a520da2d4a92a17), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 38. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let d ≥ 6, b = 64, q = N(1 − 1/b), T = 2048d, and µT = q∗T d . The average over uniform ordered lists of q distinct input labels of the total-variation distance of their outputs from a uniform injection is o(1). There is a subprobability f ≤ µT of mass 1 − o(1) and a partition into 64 equal parts for which every complementary marginal of f is bounded above by the corresponding uniform marginal. Consequently, ∥q ∗(32768d) d − UG∥TV = o(1). The full-deck conclusion holds for every deterministic starting deck.
